payload.reason: Test-only coverage slice. Reality has already settled every load-bearing question: the build check measured the gap with mutant A (935/935 green under it), spike 1 measured that the exact Fact turns the repro green and kills mutant A on Revised alone, and spike 2 measured 63 of 63 stable runs under both TEMP arms. The one proposal matches the tree as read here.
payload.selection_rationale: There was one proposal (practice). It was checked against the tree, not against taste. (1) The helpers it reuses exist and are private to TopLevelTests: Watch (TopLevelTests.cs:570), AssertSnapshotsHold (:606), Put (:738), Named (:744) and MiB (:16). So the Fact has to live in that class, as the build check said. (2) AssertSnapshotsHold already asserts `(!moved || row.Revised)` for a settled row (:667-669). Listing "a-stale.bin" in correctedRows is therefore enough to kill mutant A, and spike 1 measured exactly that failure message. (3) The repro's reader (tests/bugs/SL-105-FileRowRevisedGuard/FileRowRevisedGuardTests.cs) was checked regex by regex against the planned Fact text. RootLevelHardlink matches `Hardlink(tree.PathOf("a-stale.bin")` (no separator in the literal). GrowsTheFile matches `TempTree.Append(`. ScansARealTree matches `Watch(`. FileRow matches both `EntryKind.File` and `correctedRows: ["a-stale.bin"]`. AssertsRevisedTrue matches the literal-`true` Assert.Equal tuple. The existing folder-row Fact is excluded because its PathOf literal holds a backslash (`1-folder\stale.bin`). (4) The src it relies on behaves as claimed. Seed settles rows with Pending == 0, i.e. File and Link rows (TopLevelTracker.cs:65-68). Moved's parent walk exits at once for a root child (:118-121). Build makes every File row Done and latches Revised at :194. (5) It is the cheapest thing that works: about 30 lines in one existing file, plus committing the two source files of the repro project that the repro stage wrote. No src changes. Everything is reversible by deleting a method. The practice designer did not raise over_engineering_flag. Its cross-domain transfer (mutation testing) is kept because it defines what 'guarded' means here, and the build check and spike already measured all three of its invariants on this machine.

components.name: Root-level stale-hardlink File-row Fact
components.responsibility: Guards the file-row half of SL-063's Revised latch (O-018). A File row directly under the scan root is seeded and settled at its stale hardlink listing size, then the probe pass corrects it in place. That row must end Done at the grown size with Revised true, and the subfolder row holding the written name must stay unrevised.
components.key_interactions: Name: AnInPlaceCorrectionOfARootLevelFileNameMarksThatFileRowRevised. Insert it directly after AnInPlaceCorrectionOfAnEarlierNameIsCreditedToThatNamesRow (ends at line 108) and before TopLevelLinksAreNotFollowedRowsWithNothingCounted. Give it a /// summary in the class's style that cites O-018 and #221, says nothing may open a-stale.bin by name before the scan, and says tests/bugs/SL-105-FileRowRevisedGuard reads its shape. Body, as spike 1 measured it: `using var tree = new TempTree(); tree.Folder("sub"); string current = Put(tree, @"sub\current.bin", 1 * MiB); TempTree.Hardlink(tree.PathOf("a-stale.bin"), current); TempTree.Append(current, 63 * MiB); Watched scan = Watch(tree.Root, correctedRows: ["a-stale.bin"]);`. Asserts, in order: (1) Status is Completed. (2) scan.Result.Probes == 1. (3) `int stale = Scans.Find(scan.Result, tree.PathOf("a-stale.bin"))` and Store.Flags(stale) == SizeProbed | ProbeCorrected. (4) Named(scan.Snapshots[0], "a-stale.bin") has (Kind, State, Bytes, Revised) == (EntryKind.File, TopLevelState.Done, 1 * MiB, false). (5) `Assert.Equal((EntryKind.File, TopLevelState.Done, 64 * MiB, true), (charged.Kind, charged.State, charged.Bytes, charged.Revised))` on Named(scan.Final, "a-stale.bin"), as one statement with a literal `true` and written in the Fact's own body. (6) charged.OnDisk == scan.Result.Store.OnDisk(stale). (7) Named(scan.Final, "sub") has (State, Bytes, Files, Folders, Revised) == (TopLevelState.Done, 0L, 1L, 1L, false). Nothing between Append and Watch may touch a-stale.bin: no File.Exists, no FileInfo, no open.

key_decisions.decision: The guard is one [Fact] inside TopLevelTests. It reuses the private Watch, AssertSnapshotsHold, Put, Named and Watched unchanged: no new parameter on Watch, no helper extraction, no new test class.
key_decisions.rationale: The helpers are private to the class (TopLevelTests.cs:560-597, :738, :744). The watcher's existing `(!moved || row.Revised)` clause kills mutant A once a root-level File row is listed in correctedRows. Spike 1 measured TopLevel at 25/25 on unmutated src, and 24 pass / 1 fail under mutant A, failing on Revised.

key_decisions.decision: Fixture: sub\current.bin is written at 1 MiB, root\a-stale.bin is hardlinked to it through TempTree.Hardlink (cmd.exe mklink /H, #321), then 63 MiB are appended through the sub name. Nothing touches a-stale.bin by name before Watch.
key_decisions.rationale: This is the NTFS per-name directory-entry behaviour the investigation measured. The root listing is committed before sub is descended into, so the root name is met first: it is charged at its stale size and it is the only name probed (Probes == 1). Lesson #221: any open of the stale name refreshes its entry and destroys the scenario. Spike 2 measured snapshot 0 at 1,048,576 in 63 of 63 runs.

key_decisions.decision: Assert the stale precondition explicitly (snapshot 0: File, Done, 1 MiB, not Revised) as well as the end state.
key_decisions.rationale: If something ever refreshes the entry before Seed, the Fact fails at a line that names the cause rather than at a Revised mismatch that reads like a product regression. The Fact cannot pass vacuously either way: a refreshed entry never moves, so the final literal-true assertion would fail too.

key_decisions.decision: The final Revised assertion is one Assert.Equal tuple with a literal `true`, in the Fact's own body, after the Fact's attribute and before the next test's attribute.
key_decisions.rationale: The acceptance check recognises a positive Revised assertion by text. AssertsRevisedTrue splits on ';' and needs Assert., Revised and a lower-case true, with no Assert.False. A test unit runs from its own [Fact] to the next one, so an assertion moved into a helper defined elsewhere would not be seen. The class already uses this exact form at TopLevelTests.cs:104.
C3 was measured present: the behaviour is correct today. The defect is the missing guard, and a src change would leave nothing for mutant A to be measured against.

key_decisions.decision: Mutant A's kill is verified once, at build and again at validate, in a disposable copy following Mutants.ps1's safety discipline. No standing mutant script is committed, and SL-102's Mutants.ps1 ValidateSet roster is not extended.
key_decisions.rationale: The Fact is the standing guard. Mutants.ps1 belongs to SL-102: its ValidateSet ('All','A','B','Offline','Pinned','Unpinned') is a last-access roster, and adding a TopLevelTracker mutant there would change what SL-102's 'All' run means. #428 is honoured by never mutating the worktree.

key_decisions.decision: Commit tests/bugs/SL-105-FileRowRevisedGuard unchanged. Leave docs/design/SL-063-done-row-revised.md and SL-063's records alone.
key_decisions.rationale: The repro is the acceptance check and becomes the bug-catalog row that later validates re-run. SL-063's record is that slice's (#452), and the new Fact's /// summary carries the O-018 link.

key_decisions.decision: No KnownWorkarounds entry. The NTFS stale directory-entry behaviour is outside the project, but nothing in this slice steps around it.
key_decisions.rationale: The scanner already reads sizes from each file's own handle in the probe pass (SL-056, Q-004). That is the product's counting rule, not a toggleable workaround, and this slice only adds a test that pins it. Nothing is skipped, refused or retried.

The design changes no dependency between components. The one textual property that matters, that the Fact is never skipped, is already enforced by the fitness rule 'CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped (*.cs)' over tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/**/*.cs. A regex for this one mutant's spelling in TopLevelTracker.cs would under-fence (#446) and duplicate the behavioural guard.

proposals.note: The only proposal. Taken whole. Its code claims were checked against the tree, its Fact body matches spike 1's measured diff, and the repro's regexes were checked against the planned text. Two wording changes: the catalog re-run is credited to the mechanism Q-249 describes (labelled recalled), and the mutant-kill check is spelled out as an unattended command sequence so validate can settle C2.

payload.coherence_check: One proposal, so there is no composition to check. Nothing in this design has yet survived a disagreement with another designer, and the reviewer downstream is the first to argue with it. What was checked instead is the seams inside the single design. (a) The Fact against the acceptance reader: every one of the five regexes in FileRowRevisedGuardTests.cs matches the planned Fact text. The literal-true tuple sits in the Fact's own unit, from its [Fact] to TopLevelLinksAreNotFollowedRowsWithNothingCounted's [Fact], and the comment-stripping pass blanks the /// summary, so prose there cannot satisfy or break the reader. (b) The Fact against the watcher: under mutant A, Watch's AssertSnapshotsHold throws before the explicit asserts run, so the failure text is the watcher's ('row a-stale.bin: Revised is False, its figures moved'). That is the message spike 1 recorded, so the explicit asserts and the watcher do not contradict each other. (c) The Fact against fitness rules over tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/** (never skipped, no cloud-files calls, no %SystemRoot%\Temp fixture, interop only in TestNative): a plain [Fact] built through TempTree meets all of them. (d) The committed repro against fitness rules over tests/**: it has no DllImport and no SMB, Defender or registry writes, and no rule fences Directory.EnumerateFiles or File.ReadAllText under tests/bugs. (e) Lesson #388 (a 'one Fact' change undercounts its edit): nothing under tests/ pins TopLevelTests' method names (grep for nameof(TopLevelTests / TopLevelTests. / "TopLevelTests" found none), no pinned array is involved, and the diff is one edited .cs file plus two new repro source files. The default suite goes from 935 to 936. (f) Q-114's WindowMutants requirement is keyed on src/FsAnalyser.Core/TopLevel*.cs, and this diff touches only tests/, so it does not apply. architecture_rules is empty on purpose: the design settles no dependency boundary, and the one property worth enforcing textually is already a rule.

code_claims.claim: A private static helper. It scans with TopLevelInterval = TimeSpan.Zero, records progress.TopLevel after every listing through AfterFolder, appends the final snapshot, and calls AssertSnapshotsHold with the given correctedRows.

For a row after the snapshot it settled in, it asserts `(!moved || row.Revised)`, that Revised never goes back to false, and that a row not in correctedRows is never Revised. It also asserts a row is not Revised in the snapshot it settles in.
Builds the stale-hardlink shape with the stale name at 1-folder\stale.bin and asserts `(charged.Revised, repeat.Revised) == (true, false)` over folder rows only.
A private helper that creates the parent folder of a relative path and then a file of the given length, returning its path.
A private helper that returns the single row with the given name from a TopLevelSnapshot.
The [Fact] that directly follows AnInPlaceCorrectionOfAnEarlierNameIsCreditedToThatNamesRow, so the new Fact's source unit ends at its attribute.
Builds one row per root child with Pending = 1 only for folders, and calls Settle on every row whose Pending is 0. File and Link rows are therefore settled at their listed size.
Walks the corrected record's parents up to the root to find its row. For a direct child of the root the loop exits at once and the bytes are added to that child's own row.

Gives every File row the Done state and every Link row NotFollowed. It latches Revised when the state is Done and (Bytes, OnDisk) differ from (SettledBytes, SettledOnDisk). Mutant A gates this latch with `r.Kind != EntryKind.File &&`.
Copies a row's Bytes and OnDisk into SettledBytes and SettledOnDisk.
The probe-credit path calls _topLevel.Moved(entry, posted.Size, posted.OnDisk) only when the correction is in place.
The tracker is seeded when the root listing commits (row == RootRow).
Creates a second name for an existing file by running cmd.exe /c mklink /H newName existing, and returns newName.
Opens the path with FileMode.Append and FileAccess.Write and writes the requested number of bytes through that name.
When the temp path is at or under the Windows folder, puts test trees in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests instead, so the fixture never lands in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP.
Returns the store index of the record at a given full path in a ScanResult.
Passes once a [Fact]/[Theory] unit under tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests matches all of these: RootLevelHardlink, GrowsTheFile, ScansARealTree, FileRow and AssertsRevisedTrue. Today it fails at line 99.
Matches Hardlink( whose first argument is x.PathOf("name") or Path.Combine(root, "name"), where the name holds no separator.
Counts a ';'-separated statement as a positive Revised assertion when it contains Assert. and Revised, has no Assert.False, and has a lower-case `true` or an Assert.True( with no '!'.
Matches EntryKind.File, or a correctedRows: ["..."] whose first name holds a dot and no separator.
A fitness rule over tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/**/*.cs that forbids Skip on [Fact]/[Theory], Assert.Skip and Explicit = true, so the new Fact is covered by it.
Its -Mutant parameter is a fixed SL-102 roster ('All','A','B','Offline','Pinned','Unpinned') with no entry for TopLevelTracker.
The one existing root-level stale-hardlink test. It is not Watch-based and never asserts TopLevel or Revised.

contracts.name: SL-105 acceptance command
contracts.notes: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/bugs/SL-105-FileRowRevisedGuard/SL-105-FileRowRevisedGuard.Tests.csproj` exits 0. The default suite (`eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx`) goes from 935 to 936 and stays green.
contracts.error_cases: Goes red again if the Fact is reshaped so the reader no longer recognises it. Examples: the Revised assertion moves into a helper defined outside the Fact's unit; it becomes Assert.True with a '!'; the root path is built with a separator inside the PathOf literal; or Hardlink or Append is renamed.

contracts.name: TopLevelTests.AnInPlaceCorrectionOfARootLevelFileNameMarksThatFileRowRevised
contracts.notes: A plain [Fact] with no Trait and no Skip, so the default VSTestTestCaseFilter runs it and CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped covers it. The tree is built only through TempTree, so it lands in %TEMP%\fsa-tests, or in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests when TEMP is under the Windows folder. It is removed on Dispose. About 67 ms.
contracts.error_cases: A refreshed directory entry fails at the snapshot-0 assertion (64 MiB, not 1 MiB). A kind-gated latch fails inside Watch with 'row a-stale.bin: Revised is False, its figures moved in snapshot N'. A correction credited to the wrong row fails the watcher's `(corrected || !row.Revised)` on sub, or the sub assertion.

cross_domain_transfer.pattern: A coverage test is accepted when it kills a named mutant: one fault, red on that test only, red for the stated reason, and green on unmodified code.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: The gap was exposed by a surviving mutant, so it closes when that mutant dies. The acceptance repro reads source text and could be satisfied by a test with the right words and the wrong behaviour. The mutant-kill case is what ties the words to the behaviour.

NTFS hardlink directory-entry semantics (per-name size cache, refreshed when the name is opened)

outside_claims.claim: On NTFS, a write through one hardlink name updates the size only in that name's directory entry. Another name's entry, as a directory listing returns it, keeps the old size.
outside_claims.source: Investigation NTFS probe on C: (root listing 1048576, sub listing 4194304). Spike 2: snapshot-0 a-stale.bin = 1,048,576 in 63 of 63 runs
outside_claims.if_wrong: Seed would charge 64 MiB, the row would never move, and the Fact would fail at its snapshot-0 assertion. The fixture would need another way to make a stale entry.

outside_claims.claim: Opening the stale name, or querying it by name, refreshes its directory entry to the current size.
outside_claims.source: Investigation NTFS probe (root listing read 4194304 after the by-name query); lesson #221 (SL-045: 0 to 256 MiB)
outside_claims.if_wrong: Nothing breaks. The design's rule 'never touch a-stale.bin before Watch' would just be a stricter precaution than needed.

outside_claims.claim: cmd.exe mklink /H creates a hardlink as an ordinary user, without elevation or Developer Mode.
outside_claims.source: Spikes 1 and 2 ran the Fact unelevated through TempTree.Hardlink; existing HardlinkTests run in the default suite
outside_claims.if_wrong: The Fact would fail in setup. It is never skipped (Q-001's rule).

outside_claims.claim: The engine runs validate with TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP.
outside_claims.source: Lessons #371/#390/#391; spike 2 ran an arm under it

prior_art.pattern: Judge a test by the mutants it kills. A surviving mutant marks a branch no test reaches, and the fix is a test that kills it while passing on the original code.
On NTFS, a write through one hardlink name updates size and attributes only in that name's directory entry, so correct sizes come from the file itself, not the listing.
prior_art.where: Microsoft Learn, 'Hard links and junctions' (as quoted by this slice's investigation; not in this run's fetched block)

prior_art.pattern: Assert the fixture's precondition before the behaviour, so an environment that silently destroys the scenario fails loudly instead of passing vacuously.
prior_art.where: Common real-filesystem test practice; this repo's lesson #221 (HeldOpenTreeTests B1)

taste_disagreements: Where the mutant-A kill lives. Chosen: a one-off check in a disposable copy at build and validate, following Mutants.ps1's safety discipline but adding nothing to it. Alternative: add a TopLevelTracker entry to SL-102's Mutants.ps1 ValidateSet roster so the kill is repeatable. Lesson #428 says 'apply mutants only through Mutants.ps1'. Against that, the roster is SL-102's last-access set, and widening it changes what SL-102's 'All' run means.

Whether the Fact belongs in HardlinkTests, next to ALoneNameUnderTheRootIsChargedAtItsOwnSize, which already builds the root-level stale shape. It is placed in TopLevelTests because Watch and its watcher are private there, and the guarded behaviour is the top-level row, not the hardlink charge.
